messages:
carmen_sales: Quick ask-- Prospect Helix wants a 2-week proof-of-concept. They need hosted API keys for a team of ~15 data engineers, and they prefer keys that can be rotated by their admin daily. Any standard pattern we should follow?

rekha_se: For hosted POCs we offer ephemeral tokens with configurable TTLs and a rotation endpoint. Typical flow: create token, share via secure link, set per-token rate limits + monthly cap, and enable audit logging.

carmen_sales: Do we have a self-service rotation API so they can call it themselves?

ben_devops: We expose a customer-facing rotation endpoint for Dedicated customers, but for hosted POCs we generally rotate on their behalf to avoid secret management errors. If Helix insists on self-rotation, we can whitelist a callback URL and give them a scoped "rotator" token that only calls /rotate.

rekha_se: Example rotator call (internal pattern):
```
POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/keys/rotate
Headers: Authorization: Bearer <rotator-token>
Body: {"key_id":"k_abc123","new_ttl_seconds":86400}
```
Response returns new secret (one-time). We recommend using short lifetimes (<=7d) when customer data is sensitive.

ben_devops: Note: rotator tokens themselves must be long-lived on our side to support automation, but they are scope-limited (action:rotate only, org_id bound). We log every rotate action to audit and forward to SIEM.

carmen_sales: Security asked if we can require IP restrictions per token. Helix will provide CIDR ranges.

tom_security: Yes require IP allowlist. Also require tagging metadata: `x-purpose: poc`, `x-owner: carmen`, `x-customer: helix`. If the POC ingests production traces, reduce TTL to 72h and require S3 audit export.

rekha_se: We'll create two token classes for this POC: "poc-standard" TTL=7d and "poc-sensitive" TTL=3d. Both support IP allowlist and per-token spend caps. We'll provision 15 tokens under org helix-987.

carmen_sales: If they ask how to rotate mid-POC, what's the play-by-play?

ben_devops: Rotation procedure we follow: 1) Create replacement token with identical scopes and metadata, 2) deliver new secret via secure share link, 3) update any webhook/clients, 4) call revoke on old token, 5) confirm no active usage. We timestamp everything in the ticket.

rekha_se: Revoke example:
```
POST https://internal-admin.redwood/api/v1/keys/k_oldtoken/revoke
-H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN"
-d '{"reason":"rotation by customer","actor":"carmen_sales"}'
```
Event emitted: `key.revoked` (fields: key_id, org_id, actor, reason, ts).

ops-bot: :white_check_mark: Created keys: k_poc_helix_01 .. k_poc_helix_15 (provisioned with IP allowlist pending CIDRs).

carmen_sales: Can we attach a spend guard to each token? Theyre worried about someone running experiments that cost a lot.

ben_devops: Yes. Per-token spend cap and hard throttle are supported. Default for POC is $200 total per token for the 2-week window. We also set alerts at 50/75/90% to carmen and billing.

tom_security: Add SIEM enrollment and S3 audit export to the ticket. Also mark tokens with `sensitivity: high` if they ingest customer identifiable info.

carmen_sales: Thanks. One more  if Helix later wants to move to a Dedicated pool, will the hosted POC tokens stop working?

rekha_se: Tokens remain valid until revoked. For migration we normally create new tokens under the Dedicated org and deprecate hosted tokens. We advise creating cutover plan: issue new tokens, update clients, revoke old ones.

carmen_sales: Great. Please add a short runbook to the SF ticket with the creation, rotate, revoke steps and whom to ping. I'll collect CIDRs from Helix and confirm whether PII will be used.

ops-bot: :memo: Runbook added to ticket SF-5598: https://redwood.internal/t/SF-5598

ben_devops: I'll provision keys with TTL=3d for any dataset flagged PII; otherwise 7d. Will wait on CIDRs.

carmen_sales: Thanks all. I'll update Helix and close the loop once they confirm CIDRs and PII status. :thumbsup:
